column5: Look: everything ASCII on a canvas character grid in one crisp monospace font. Terrain shaded with a long character-density ramp, hillshaded by the current sun azimuth/elevation, with long real cast shadows at low sun; pitch-black shadowed crater with faint blue `·` frost. Limited palette: 5–6 greys for regolith, amber/white for the Sun and lit faces, blue/white Earth, phosphor-green UI, black star field, subtle CRT glow and scanlines. Box-drawing borders, gauges as `[████░░]`, hand-made ASCII title logo. Signature detail: a detailed ASCII Earth disc showing its phase hanging over the skyline strip, and sun glare streaks when the Sun clips a ridge. Animated dish and panels tracking Earth and Sun, footprints, landing dust, transmit pulse. Every figure drawn in characters: no images, no emoji, no plain circles.
References: the real lunar south pole (Shackleton rim, Connecting Ridge, the low sun) *(guessed)*; classic roguelike ASCII readability *(guessed)*.
View: 2D · Camera: top-down map, with a 360° skyline panorama strip above it.
Orbit scout: ASCII map of the site, a live 360° skyline from the scout's position, up to 3 flags with each site's sunlit % and Earth visibility, time scrub to preview the sky, then land.
Horizon sky model: placeholder Sun and Earth tracks (low Sun circling, Earth wobbling) occluded by the heightmap horizon; instrument bar with sun elevation, time to sunset/Earthset, Earth visibility.

Turn-based surface: steps and work cost mission time; five stations: hab, solar array (low-power wait), survey (needs Sun), drill (needs battery reserve, pays more in the shadowed crater), dish (needs Earth); battery drains in the dark and cold.
Three short missions: learn the horizon, get science home, the trade-off; Mission 3's 12-hour launch slip sends you back to orbit to re-pick or hold; radio messages from mission control.
ASCII art pass: hillshade, cast shadows, crater frost, phased Earth disc, sun glare, animated dish and panels, footprints, landing dust, transmit pulse, CRT glow, ASCII title, HUD and end screens.
Synthesized sound and generative music that follow the sky (warm in Sun, cold in shadow, home layer while Earth is visible, tension near set); mute toggle.

The title logo types itself in with typewriter clicks and radio static.
Mission 1 opens in orbit over the site: the skyline strip shows the Sun sitting just above a ridge, and the hint reads "Move the scout.
Watch the sky."
Moving one way, the Sun sinks behind a ridge and the map's shadows swing; the other way, it clears.
The player plants a flag where the Sun is clear and presses Enter.
Landing dust, a thump, the hab appears.
They step to the survey station and press E: science ticks up while the instrument bar shows SUN VISIBLE.
A few turns later the Sun's track nears a ridge shoulder, the bar turns amber, "SUNSET 6h", and the music thins and turns cold.
The ridge, not the clock, is what ends the day.
Mission 1 is gentle: one sunset around minute 3, and enough battery to wait it out at the array.
Mission 2 adds Earthset: science you collected but have not transmitted is worth nothing until you send it before Earth slips behind the ridge.
Mission 3 is the full trade-off: the shadowed terrace pays most but drains the battery in the cold, and a 12-hour launch slip moves the whole sky.
If the battery hits zero, the mission ends early and you keep only what was transmitted.
Each mission ends at its departure time.
*(provisional, from "in between")*
